definition: Rows in the public 311 yearly files vs distinct REQUESTID; ids appearing more than once
label: observed
derivation: Counted rows and distinct REQUESTIDs in the city's 2024, 2025 and 2026 CSB files. Repeated rows are identical except CALLERTYPE, so they look like one row per caller; we keep one row per request.
note: Medians computed on rows weight multi-caller requests; dedupe before any count or median.

definition: Mean DATETIMECLOSED-DATETIMEINIT over STATUS=CLOSED requests closed by 30 Jun 2026, all channels, ward 1
label: observed
derivation: 311 requests (csb.zip), one row per REQUESTID, all channels and types, filed in CityStat's window; mean days to close for requests closed by the window end. CityStat publishes 17.18 for ward 1 (tableau-extract.md).
note: A July 2026 snapshot (closed by 10 Jul) gives 17.36; see decomposition.

definition: How closely our definition reproduces CityStat's 14 ward averages
label: observed
derivation: Compared our ward means (one row per REQUESTID, all channels, mean over closed requests) with CityStat's CSBRequestMap values extracted 13 Oct 2026. Ward request counts match within 1% once duplicate rows are removed (about 8% high without that).
note: Our window total 285,582 distinct requests vs CityStat 286,148. Wards 10-12 are 2-3 days lower in ours.

definition: CityStat's metric: ward 10 mean days to close minus ward 1
label: observed
derivation: 311 requests (csb.zip), one row per REQUESTID, all channels, as CityStat counts them; ward 1 17.4 vs ward 10 33.1 days (CityStat shows 17.2 vs 35.1).

unit: mean days (share of gap in note)
definition: Part of the ward 1 vs ward 10 gap due to mix of request types
label: observed
derivation: 311 requests (csb.zip), one row per REQUESTID, all channels; closures classed by their closing words (N2's reviewed classes). Exact two-level split of the mean gap: type mix, then share of each closing class within type, then speed within the same type and class.

unit: mean days (share of gap in note)
definition: Part of the ward 1 vs ward 10 gap due to closing words used (class shares within type)
label: observed
derivation: 311 requests (csb.zip), one row per REQUESTID, all channels; closures classed by their closing words (N2's reviewed classes). Exact two-level split of the mean gap: type mix, then share of each closing class within type, then speed within the same type and class.

unit: mean days (share of gap in note)
definition: Part of the ward 1 vs ward 10 gap due to slower handling, closures recording work done
label: observed
derivation: 311 requests (csb.zip), one row per REQUESTID, all channels; closures classed by their closing words (N2's reviewed classes). Exact two-level split of the mean gap: type mix, then share of each closing class within type, then speed within the same type and class.

unit: mean days (share of gap in note)
definition: Part of the ward 1 vs ward 10 gap due to slower handling, hand-off / no-action / other closures
label: observed
derivation: 311 requests (csb.zip), one row per REQUESTID, all channels; closures classed by their closing words (N2's reviewed classes). Exact two-level split of the mean gap: type mix, then share of each closing class within type, then speed within the same type and class.

definition: Same decomposition with enforcement notices (N2 rule handed_off:enforcement) as their own class
label: observed
derivation: As n3_decomp_ward1_vs_10_*, but notices of violation, 'already under notice' and summons are separated from other hand-offs; the split barely moves.
note: Mix + closing words 2.2 of 15.7 days with the split, 1.9 without.

definition: Type-mix term, wards 1-5 vs 10-14 (negative = the north files a faster-closing mix)
label: observed
derivation: Same decomposition for wards 1-5 vs 10-14: the north's mix of request types would make it faster, not slower; its gap is all within-type.
note: Gap 7.6 d = mix -3.2 + closing words 0.9 + speed (done) 1.7 + speed (other) 8.1.

definition: Ward 10's median days to close if it had ward 1's mix of request types and closing words (reweighted)
label: observed
derivation: 311 requests (csb.zip), one row per REQUESTID, all channels; ward 10's closures reweighted to ward 1's type-by-closing-class shares.
note: Observed: ward 10 5.9, ward 1 2.8. Matching the mix does not shrink the gap.

definition: Median days from filing to a closure reading "vehicle tagged for tow"
label: observed
derivation: 311 requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid bytes dropped), one row per REQUESTID; resident-filed requests only (web, phone, email, chat, Twitter, letter). Compared only closures with the same closing words, "vehicle tagged for tow", which needs a visit; the city's promise for every towing request is 5 days.
note: Before the tornado: 16.0 vs 36.1 (n 578/266). All five north wards slower than every ward 1-5 after the tornado.

definition: Share of towing requests closed (any words) by the city's own promise date; open and cancelled count as not
label: observed
derivation: 311 requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid bytes dropped), one row per REQUESTID; resident-filed requests only (web, phone, email, chat, Twitter, letter). Promise = PRJCOMPLETEDATE, set by the city on each request (5 days for towing); only requests whose promise date had passed by 13 Oct 2026.
note: Retired for public use 14 Oct 2026 (N8 conflict 1): counts closures with any words, so 'vehicle gone upon inspection', 'no problem found' and blank closings count as kept promises. Use n3_towing_tagged_by_promise_after, the same population and closing words as the 12.0 vs 36.9-day medians.

definition: Share of towing requests closed "vehicle tagged for tow" whose closing time is at or before the city's own promise date (PRJCOMPLETEDATE, 5 days)
label: observed
derivation: 311 requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip 2025 and 2026 yearly CSVs, invalid bytes dropped: build/csb-clean), one row per REQUESTID, resident-filed if any of its rows has a resident CALLERTYPE (web, phone, email, chat, Twitter, letter); towing requests filed on or after 16 May 2025, STATUS CLOSED with PUBLICRESOLUTION 'vehicle tagged for tow' (the inspector's first visit, the same population as the 12.0 vs 36.9-day medians); share whose DATETIMECLOSED is at or before PRJCOMPLETEDATE; wards from the WARD column, 1-5 against 10-14.
note: 414 of 1,300 and 10 of 271 requests (the north figure rests on about 10 requests). By calendar date instead of timestamp: 32.3% vs 4.8%. Replaces N3's earlier share counting any closing words (38% vs 11%, now retired). N8 conflict 1 reproduced 31.8% vs 3.7%.

definition: Median days to a closure reading "vehicle gone upon inspection"
label: observed
derivation: 311 requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid bytes dropped), one row per REQUESTID; resident-filed requests only (web, phone, email, chat, Twitter, letter). Same closing words both sides; a long wait here means the inspection came after the car left.

definition: Median days to "referred to street maintenance for repair work to be scheduled", cave-ins
label: observed
derivation: 311 requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid bytes dropped), one row per REQUESTID; resident-filed requests only (web, phone, email, chat, Twitter, letter). Same closing words both sides. Per ward the line falls between ward 5 (under 1.2 days in every ward 1-5) and ward 6 (over 15 days in every ward 6-14), which points to a different intake process, not only slower crews.
note: Inferred: in wards 1-5 the referral is made at intake; in 6-14 after an inspection wait. Repair dates for referred cave-ins are not in the file.

definition: Median days to a closure recording the work as done ("work completed"), cave-ins
label: observed
derivation: 311 requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid bytes dropped), one row per REQUESTID; resident-filed requests only (web, phone, email, chat, Twitter, letter). Only closures whose words record the repair; referrals excluded because in wards 1-5 they happen within a day whatever the repair date.
note: South n is 35: too few for the robustness rule (n >= 100).

definition: Single light out, median days to "work completed"
label: observed
derivation: 311 requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid bytes dropped), one row per REQUESTID; resident-filed requests only (web, phone, email, chat, Twitter, letter). Only closures recording the repair. City promise 3 days.
note: Not robust: the gap sits in two quarters (filed Oct 2025-Mar 2026: 20 vs 49 and 5 vs 31 days); other quarters are level.

definition: Exterior property-maintenance complaints: median days to "issued notice of violation"
label: observed
derivation: 311 requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid bytes dropped), one row per REQUESTID; resident-filed requests only (web, phone, email, chat, Twitter, letter). Same closing words both sides; promise 14 days.
note: Absolute gap about 5 days, inside the promise; slowness concentrated in wards 9-12 (11-22 days); ward 13 (4.7) is faster than ward 4 (8.8).

definition: Done-class median days for high-volume types with no material ward gap
label: observed
derivation: 311 requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid bytes dropped), one row per REQUESTID; resident-filed requests only (web, phone, email, chat, Twitter, letter). Only closures whose words record the work as done.

definition: Share of closures where N3's independent first-pass rules give the same class as N2's reviewed classes
label: observed
derivation: Two independent classifications of the city's closing words (N2's reviewed list; N3's rules), compared closure-weighted; enforcement notices counted as hand-offs as N2 does.
